calls.head: Nowhere to hide for Suzuki
calls.body: At home, the Bruins keep sending Lindholm’s line (Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Hagens) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Marco Sturm has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Canadiens’ first line is Caufield, Suzuki and Slafkovský.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Canadiens take down the Bruins
paras: Kirby Dach struck first for the Canadiens early in the first, and Josh Anderson made it 2-0 midway through the period. The second period belonged to the Canadiens: Jake Evans scored, Cole Caufield scored, and Phillip Danault scored to make it 5-0. Boston pulled Jeremy Swayman after four goals and turned to Michael DiPietro for the rest of the second. Casey Mittelstadt got the Bruins on the board midway through the second, and he struck again just 53 seconds into the third to make it 5-2. Mike Matheson was back in the lineup after missing six games, and picked up an assist.

The chances were closer than the score. Jacob Fowler made 30 saves for the Canadiens. He has earned a point in eleven straight starts (9-0-2). By our Swing measure, Elias Lindholm had the best night of anyone, even in a loss. The Habs improved to 12-3-4 and climbed to second in the Atlantic, while the Bruins fell to 13-5-1, slipping out of first in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Canadiens have points in twelve straight games (9-0-3), the longest run in the league right now.
